newsitem.title: FRANCE: Morgan Stanley cuts LVMH to underperform.
newsitem.headline: Morgan Stanley cuts LVMH to underperform.

text.p: Brokerage Morgan Stanley said it cut its rating on LVMH Moet Hennessy Louis Vuitton to underperform from neutral on Friday on the view that the best possible outcome for a three-way deal with Guinness and Grand Metropolitan has been priced into the stock.
"The best scenario has been priced in," said analyst Sylvain Massot.
LVMH's stock was down 0.98 percent at 1,622 francs at 1022 GMT. It hit an all-time high of 1,660 on Thursday.
Before the Guinness-Grand Met merger plan was announced in May, Massot's 12-month objective for LVMH's stock was 1,450 francs.

"Under the best scenario, with LVMH getting 31 percent of UDV-MH (a merger of the three companies' drinks businesses), the value would rise 15 percent, to 1,670 francs. The market has anticipated at least the best solution," he said.
An accord between the three companies, whose chairmen met this week in Paris, does not seem within easy reach, he said.
"The two sides are very far apart. An accord will require a lot of compromise," he said.

Massot is among the analysts who feels that LVMH's proposal for a stand-alone, listed drinks business is not necessarily more advantageous to the Guinness and Grand Met shareholders than the British companies' proposed merger.

He also said "bad surprises" could not be excluded, such as a breakdown in negotiations that could prompt LVMH to buy more shares in Grand Met. It has spent more than eight billion francs since mid-June to build a 6.4 percent stake in Grand Met as part of an effort to block the proposed merger.

After Wednesday's meeting, the chairmen of the British companies said they had agreed to study LVMH chairman Bernard Arnault's proposal to set up an independent, listed company grouping their respective drinks businesses.
They asked Arnault to send them details of his plan in writing and he is expected to do so early next week.
